newsitem.title: USA: Clinton backs ban on cigarette ads that hurt kids.
newsitem.headline: Clinton backs ban on cigarette ads that hurt kids.

text.p: President Clinton on Tuesday reaffirmed his determination to ban cigarette advertising that endangers children's lives.

"We must ... protect our children by standing firm in our determination to ban the advertising and marketing of cigarettes that endanger their lives," Clinton said in his prepared State of the Union address.

Under rules unveiled by the Food and Drug Administration last year, vending machines that sell cigarettes will be banned from places teenagers can go, and billboards advertising cigarettes would be prohibited within 1,000 feet (300 metres) of schools and playgrounds.
Sales or giveways of products like caps or gym bags that carry cigarette or smokeless tobacco brand names or logos would also be prohibited.
The rules will be phased in over two years.
